questions.question: Where is the text that gets sent to a running coding worker when the supervisor decides to steer it built, based on the probabilities for AGENTS.md drift, work off track and worker stuck? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: steering.py:7 build_steering_message reads result.probability for agents_md_drift, work_off_track, worker_stuck; called from runtime.py:482 in _apply.

questions.question: Which function parses pytest result summary lines (passed/failed counts) out of a worker's captured stdout/stderr text, and in which file does it live? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: test_summary.py:96 parse_pytest_summaries; used at observation.py:404 to fill test_results.

questions.question: Where does the factory pick the single winning directive out of everything the responsibilities proposed (by priority, then confidence) and convert a retry/start request into an escalation when the worker or retry limit is hit? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: policy.py:47 FactoryPolicy.evaluate uses max() on (priority, confidence) at ~79 and downgrades RETRY_WORKER/START_VERIFIER/START_WORKER to ESCALATE (lines ~90-113).

questions.question: Where is the concrete worker object (deepagents, opencode, hermes, codex app-server or plain codex) chosen from the configuration when the factory starts a worker without a custom factory? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: runtime.py:167 _default_worker_factory branches on config.worker_backend and config.codex_backend; assigned as default at runtime.py:~107.

questions.question: Trace what happens when `foreman hook` receives the user's first submitted prompt from an assistant: from the CLI command through adapter parsing to how responsibilities get selected for that prompt. Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: cli.py:295 hook calls hook_adapter(client) (hook_adapters.py:293), builds AttachedWorkerRuntime (hooks.py:349), run_hook -> handle (hooks.py:373) -> _route_prompt (hooks.py:416/471) -> resolve_hierarchical_routing (routing.py:218, called hooks.py:475).

questions.question: In FactoryRuntime, starting from _watch_loop, trace how an assessment turns into a steering message delivered to a worker: which methods assess, which pick the directive, and which build and deliver the message. Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: runtime.py:567 _assess -> policy.evaluate (runtime.py:~438, policy.py:47); runtime.py:572 _apply -> STEER_WORKER branch calls build_steering_message (runtime.py:482) then worker.steer (workers/base.py:63).

questions.question: When the codex CLI worker exits non-zero because of a bad model/configuration error, how does the factory end up escalating without needing the semantic assessment to say so? Trace from the worker's output parsing to the escalating directive. Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: workers/codex.py:161 sets record.configuration_error via model_configuration_error (codex_errors.py:17); runtime.py:392 _assess calls policy.configuration_error (policy.py:39) which returns an ESCALATE directive with priority 1000.

questions.question: Suppose the evidence sent to the decision model is too big to fit the byte budget even after compaction. Trace how that error propagates during a factory assessment and what the runtime then does about it (including how repeated failures are handled). Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: request_budget.py:199 raises RequestBudgetError; foreman/decision.py:86-87 converts it to ForemanModelError; runtime.py:410 catches it, tolerates up to config.max_consecutive_assessment_failures with CONTINUE, then ESCALATE.

questions.question: How does the CLI decide which decision-model implementation (and request budget class) is used for the supervisor model and the responsibility router, based on configuration? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: cli.py:103 _decision_components picks OpenAIRequestBudget or JevRequestBudget by decision_provider; returns JevForemanModel/JevResponsibilityRouter or DecisionForemanModel/DecisionResponsibilityRouter (cli.py:117-128).

questions.question: Which methods call resolve_hierarchical_routing, i.e. what would need updating if its signature changed? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: runtime.py:143 in FactoryRuntime._route_work and hooks.py:475 in AttachedWorkerRuntime._route_prompt.

questions.question: If ForemanModelError changed meaning (e.g. a subclass for timeouts), which runtime-side code paths catch it and react, so would need review? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: Caught in runtime.py:410 (FactoryRuntime._assess) and hooks.py:604 (AttachedWorkerRuntime._assess_event); also raised/re-raised in foreman/decision.py:30-123.

questions.question: Which places build the default built-in responsibility registry (the function that assembles the built-in checks from config)? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: Defined responsibilities/builtin.py:362 builtin_registry; called policy.py:20 (FactoryPolicy.__post_init__), runtime.py:88 (FactoryRuntime.__init__), responsibilities/configuration.py:217 (configured_registry).

questions.question: If run_command_evidence (the helper that runs one configured evidence command) changed its return type, which functions that call it directly would break? Name the files and functions involved.
questions.notes: Direct callers: evidence.py:220 inside run_command_evidence_providers (itself used by hooks.py:573) and runtime.py:290 inside FactoryRuntime._run_worker.
